RECOMMEND: APPROVE — advance to spec.

Why: this is a small, well-grounded extension of 061's already-proven tooling, both of your decisions are settled rather than open, and the seed correctly carries forward every hazard 061 and 060 found — the PII constraint, the credential facts, and the confirmation that 2022 has no prepayment complication. This revision also adds your own stated reasoning for the combined-import call, so the entity records WHY, not just what.

DECISION EFFECT: approve advances 062 to spec, which writes the specification for a combined 2022 import — regular expenses and mortgage together, so 2022 never appears in the app as a partial year. Reject holds it at ideation.

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so spec is not re-litigating your decisions: mortgage folds into this entity rather than landing separately, because your own reasoning — a mortgage-only partial year would misrepresent 2022 in every Reports screen that reads it — is now recorded explicitly rather than just the outcome; 2022 has no principal prepayment, so 064's prepayment question does not recur here; column J is the payment source, dated by column D, same as 064, on the same reasoning that keeps 2022-2024 measured consistently with your existing 2025 record.

ONE THING WORTH YOUR ATTENTION AT SPEC, NOT NOW: this entity's own open question is whether 2022 repeats the same monthly-formula boundary errors 061 found in 2023 and 2024 (five of twelve months per year, same pattern both years). If it does, spec should tell you before you read any 2022 totals, the same courtesy 061 eventually earned for 2023-2024.

BOTH CREDENTIALS READ THE MORTGAGE SHEET, unlike the archive workbook where only staging does. Worth knowing this is a fact about who you shared the sheet with, not about the code — it would break silently if that sharing ever changed.

artifacts.summary:
SEED OUTCOME, now settled, with the captain's own reasoning recorded: import 2022 as a single combined pass — regular Daily-tab expenses and the year's twelve mortgage payments together — so 2022 never exists in the app as a partial year. She was asked base-then-mortgage versus one combined import and chose combined explicitly, because a mortgage-only year would misrepresent 2022 in every Reports screen that reads it. Named here as her stated reason, not treated as scope creep.

INCLUDED SCOPE: 2022's Daily-tab records (same 26-row band shape as 2023/2024, rows 63-88) plus 2022's twelve mortgage payments (column J of the House tab, dated by column D).

EXCLUDED SCOPE: any year other than 2022 (060 owns 2006-2025 analysis); 2023-2024 mortgage (entity 064); re-touching 061's already-imported 2023-2024 rows; any new app UI; fixing the captain's workbook formula bugs (061 Finding 6 documents them; repair is hers).

WHAT PRIOR ENTITIES ALREADY ESTABLISH, so spec does not re-derive it:
- The band is known: rows 63-88 of the Daily tab, byte-identical taxonomy to 2023/2024. 061's extractor already discovers it and currently excludes it by a --years-equivalent flag spec should verify by exercising, not trust from the note.
- Access is solved for the archive workbook: staging reads, production 403, 061's two-credential design handles it.
- 061's tooling shape should extend, not be duplicated. extract-historical-expenses.js / import-historical-expenses.js already implement the human-approval-between-read-and-write split. Since this import now spans TWO sources per year (Daily tab and House tab), spec should propose one normalization sheet fed by both, extending the existing tooling — that shape is spec's call, not decided here.
- The House tab is fully characterized already, cite rather than re-read: workbook Coast FIRE_ijac.wei, spreadsheet 1oUCppCwkfw2BMG8gZwxb13Vq8KVXBQFrVoS57ZH9h6E, tab gid 1358685274, 255 rows x 28 cols, data from row 5. Column J (actual monthly payment) numeric, 209 typed literals / 31 formulas. Column D (repayment date) adjacent, populated every row. Schedule spans 2014-11-17 to 2034-10-15, 240 monthly rows, zero gaps; 2022 has exactly 12.
- 2022 has NO principal prepayment. The mortgage schedule's six prepayment dates (2015, 2020, 2021, 2023-03, twice in 2025) do not include 2022. All twelve 2022 mortgage rows are regular payments; 064's prepayment-inclusion decision does not recur here.
- Column J over interest-only (column H) is the settled column choice, with reasoning recorded, not open: a full payment is both principal and interest; only interest is real consumption. The captain was first advised interest-only, then overruled that and chose the full payment, reasoning that her own 2025 app record already holds Mortgage as a flat full-payment estimate — J keeps 2022-2024 measured consistently with what 2025 already represents.
- Both credentials read the mortgage sheet (staging AND production confirmed working), unlike the archive workbook. A single-credential design may be viable; this is a fact about the captain's sharing, to be asserted at runtime rather than assumed.
- PII hard constraint, carried forward and extended: the mortgage sheet's House tab, column A row 2, holds a bank name, branch, full account number and an account-holder personal name in one cell. Any AC this entity writes must assert falsifiably that no cell from that column reaches the app, a notes field, a report, or the repo.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR SPEC, unresolved and genuinely spec's to answer: whether 2022 repeats 061's five-of-twelve-months formula boundary errors; 2022's actual date span (do not assume a full year — 061 found 2024 was not one); whether a third-plus-mortgage year of rows stays comfortable in the app (the captain has already said Reports' year-based aggregation makes this a non-concern); and whether 061's deferred-risk findings (an unmapped taxonomy pair, AC-19's blind spot at label rows) promote under 2022's data.

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING: 4 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed across the original checklist; the addendum (captain's reasoning, tooling-shape pointer, House tab citation, column-J reasoning) was a captain/FO-directed accuracy pass made in place with the gate withdrawn, cited above with its own evidence.
